answer: Glacier-core key custody: each agent identity is bound to a hardware key sealed inside a tamper-responsive module that zeroizes on intrusion. Enrollment requires the module to perform an attested key ceremony and publish a signed freshness beacon at dawn; operators cannot export or clone the private half. A vine-like append-only log chains every beacon into a sparse Merkle tree, so a second module presenting the same identity is detectable. Attacker cost: one physical module per identity plus repeated hardware acquisition, since extraction yields no reusable secret.
